title: Advice to young clarinet students and embouchure
summary: Picou tells students to keep lips firm, and says he only ever covered the bottom teeth.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: When a young fellow comes to you to learn to play clarinet, what's the first thing you tell them?

Well, I tell them whether you... When you're blowing a clarinet, don't do this. Just puff out your cheeks and all of them. Yeah. Because something is in your mouth, you do this. Yeah. Keep your lips back there firm. Yeah. Yeah.
What do you find is the biggest trouble with the younger musicians when they try to play? What is the mistake that they make the most?
All of them. Are there some habits that are harder to break than others? Oh, yeah. I mean, what is it that you have to break them up you usually find?

No, they've got... They've got some people, if you can take a try of that, and they blow there, and they blow so nicely. How do you like that? The other ones can't blow nothing. Do you remember the TOs or any other players here that if they were the old-time clarinetists, did they ever cover both the teeth, the upper teeth too? No. Only the bottom. Only the bottom. The TOs didn't cover both. Only the bottom. Because I think Barney Bigard now changed and uses his double, what they call a double embouchure. Oh, yeah, you can do that too. But you never did do that? No, no. Always used just the teeth right on the... The bottom. Just the bottom teeth.
